# `Q-2-29` — Footnote Definition Has No Content On Its Line

> A footnote definition's text must start on the same line as its
> `[^ref]:` label; for multi-paragraph notes, use the
> `::: ^ref … :::` div syntax.

## What this means

A footnote definition was written with nothing after the colon of
its label. Quarto markdown reads a footnote's text only from the
label's own line, so none of these define the note:

```markdown
Some text[^1].

[^1]:
The text on the next line.
```

```markdown
Some text[^1].

[^1]:
    The text indented on the next line, as Pandoc allows.
```

```markdown
Some text[^1].

[^1]:
```

## Why this happens

Pandoc accepts footnote content on the lines after the label, either
as an indented block or as a lazy continuation line. Markdown copied
from a Pandoc document, or written by someone used to Pandoc, often
uses those forms. Quarto markdown does not support them.

## How to fix

For a single-paragraph note, put the text on the label's line:

```markdown
Some text[^1].

[^1]: The footnote content.
```

For a note with more than one paragraph, use the div form. The
reference inside the div (`^1` in the example) must match the
reference in the text:

```markdown
Some text[^1].

::: ^1
The first paragraph.

The second paragraph.
:::
```
